This memorandum must be given to the natural parents, guardian, any
person liable by any order or agreement to contribute to the maintenance of, or
anyone granted custody of a minor who is about to be adopted.
What Adoption Means
1. Adoption orders are made in the High Court by a Judge. It is a legal
Qn>cedme by which all your rights and duties as a parent or guardian will be
transferred to the adopters who will become the lawful parents of the minor.
This means that you will have no further rights to see the minor or to have the
minor returned to you.
Your Consent to the Adoption
2. Before the Court can make an adoption order, it has to be satisfied that
you consent of your own free will to the order being made. Consent cannot be
given before the minor is six (6) weeks old. You will be asked to sign a form of
consent which will be presented in Court as evidence of your consent. The
mother of the minor must sign her consent in the presence of a Justice of the
Peace. You are not allowed to sign a blank consent form. The proposed
adopters must either be named on the consent form or referred to by number, if
they do not wish their identity revealed to you. If they are referred to by
number you can ask what sort of people they are and you may choose, if you
want, the religious persuasions in which the minor is to be brought up.
3. The Court cannot make an adoption order, without your consent unless
you have abandoned, neglected or persistently ill-treated or seriously ill-treated
the minor, or persistently failed to discharge your parental duties, or neglected
or refused to contribute to the maintenance of the minor, or cannot be found, or
is incapable of giving consent (for instance by reason of serious mental illness)
or is unreasonably withholding consent. If one of these applies to you the Court
can dispense with your consent, and will make an adoption order.

4. You will be given notice of the hearing of the application to adopt and
will have the opportunity of making your views known to the Court if you so
wish. Where the proposed adopters are referred to by a number on the consent
form, arrangements will be made for you to attend Court at a different time.
5. The Court will appoint a person calkd the guardian ad litem who will
need to see you before the Court makes the adoption order to make sure that
you understand what the effect will be. The guardian ad litem has a duty to
ensure that an adoption order will be in the best interest of the minor and the
Court must give fist consideration to this.
6. If you sign the consent form and then, before the adoption order is
made, you wish to withdraw your consent, and want the minor back you will
have to apply to the Court for leave to remove the minor from the care of the
would-be adopters. However, you must show good cause for your decision not
to allow the adoption.
7. You are not allowed to receive or give any payment or reward in
connection with the adoption. This is an offence punishable by law.
8. The Child Care Board cannot arrange for the minor to be sent abroad for
adoption without a licence from the Chief Justice and here again the licence
cannot be granted without your consent except for one of the same sort of
reasons as are given in paragraph 3.
9. If you have taken out an insurance policy against funeral expenses for
the minor, other than one under the Friendly Societies Act, Cap. 379, the
insurers will be able to tell you whether, after the adoption order is made the
policy can be transferred to the adopters should they wish to continue it. If such
insurance was taken out under the said Act, the rights and liabilities under the
policy will after an adoption order has been made be transferred to the adopters.

be informed of these rights in order for the minor to benefit from such
entitlements.
